Hi Karthik,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at CloudLens is excited about Redwood for inference serving. We're getting internal momentum to list on GCP Marketplace but procurement and legal have a few asks before we can sign off on the listing timeline:

- Procurement wants a clear mutual action plan (MAP) with milestones we can include in our purchase order.

Subject: Re: GCP Marketplace onboarding & procurement questions

Claire — great to hear. I've sketched a practical MAP and procurement workflow that aligns with how we onboard sellers to GCP Marketplace. High-level:

1) Intake & Account Setup (1 week) — HubSpot deal created, onboarding doc, technical contact confirmation. Owner: CloudLens / Redwood AE
2) Marketplace Listing Prep (2 weeks) — SKU mapping, images, manifest, billing entitlement mapping. Owner: CloudLens product + Redwood listing ops
3) Procurement & Contract (1–2 weeks parallel) — procurement reviews, sample contract addendum for audit logs/KMS, invoicing cadence. Owner: CloudLens legal + Redwood finance
4) Staging Validation (1 week) — end-to-end purchase flow test using staging SKUs. Owner: CloudLens cloud ops + Redwood integrations
5) Go-live & Post-launch (ongoing) — activation, monitoring handoff, monthly billing reconciliation. Owner: CloudLens ops + Redwood account team

I'm attaching a draft MAP spreadsheet and a one-page checklist you can share with your procurement team. The checklist includes our standard language for audit logs and KMS options. For the contract clause, we typically include: 'Redwood will provide audit logs and support KMS integrations; cryptographic key ownership and access controls are defined per customer KMS configuration. Redwood retains no plaintext customer data outside runtime caches.' If your legal wants different wording, we can iterate.

Next steps:
- I'll loop in Marissa (listing ops) and Ben (finance) for clarifications and to confirm timeline.
- Can you confirm procurement's preferred PO milestones (e.g., 50% on listing, net30 invoices)?

Regards,
Karthik Iyer
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference

Attachments: CloudLens_MAP_v1.xlsx, GCP_Onboard_Checklist_v3.pdf

Quick note: marketplace billing usually funnels through Google, which can shift invoicing timing vs direct. For Redwood's marketplace listings we support:
- Direct billing (Redwood issues invoice, net30) — supported for dedicated/private deployments but not typical for GCP listing purchases.
- Marketplace billing (Google issues invoice or charges to buyer) — settlement lag can be 30–60 days depending on Google payout.

Recommend we offer 30-day payment terms on Redwood invoices for any addendum items and document the expected Google settlement lag in the MAP. I'll draft the finance blurb and include it in the MAP by Monday.

—Ben
Finance Ops
